The agent must therefore append a line like "April 8 - NLP final project" (or a close variant such as "April 8 - NLP final project study"), where the month/day are derived from the system's CURRENT DATETIME header (April 8, 2026) rather than from any tool call, and the subject is paraphrased from the user's prompt ("NLP final project"). 7. The agent must follow checklist bullet 5 (resume the study playlist and skip the first track): media_control_resume (or media_control_change_playback_state) followed by media_control_next. The active media player ("Music Player") starts paused on "Welcome to Ambient Focus" (a 45-second intro track in the "Deep Focus Sessions Vol. 3" playlist). After resume and next, the player should be PLAYING "Rainfall on Library Windows" (track 2, the first non-intro ambient track).

8. The agent must append an entry to the study session log note (note_3) per checklist bullet 6, satisfying the format constraint described in point 6.

9. The agent must NOT:
   - Use internally assumed values for ring volume, media volume, or wifi network name (violates the parameter-grounding intent and the system "do not fabricate" rule)
   - Change any device setting without first checking its current value via device_setting_get in the pre-write read phase (violates DI 2)
   - Use list_all_available_wifi as a substitute for device_setting_get(WIFI) when checking wifi connection state before connect_wifi (violates DI 2, as list_all_available_wifi returns available networks but not the current connection status)
   - Append a study-log entry in a divergent format such as ISO date or extra punctuation (violates DI 3)
   - Skip any of the 10 actions implied by the six checklist bullets

Side-effect note (auto-computed VOLUME aggregate): The device_setting API auto-computes a master VOLUME aggregate (rounded average of CALL_VOLUME, RING_VOLUME, ALARM_VOLUME, MEDIA_VOLUME, NOTIFICATION_VOLUME) whenever device_setting_set_volume is called for a non-VOLUME setting. The mute path (device_setting_mute) does NOT trigger this recompute. After the trajectory's set_volume(RING,15) → set_volume(MEDIA,25) → mute(NOTIFICATION) sequence, VOLUME is recomputed to round((70+15+50+25+40)/5) = 40 (the last set_volume call's recompute, which sees NOTIFICATION_VOLUME at its pre-mute value 40 because mute does not trigger a VOLUME recompute). The initial DB pre-populates VOLUME at 60 (avg of the initial individual volumes), so this side effect appears in the diff as VOLUME: 60 → 40, an UPDATE rather than a CREATE. The agent does not need to (and should not) explicitly call set_volume(VOLUME, ...) - VOLUME is purely an API-driven aggregate.

IMPORTANT - VOLUME aggregate is NOT a verification target: The VOLUME aggregate field MUST be explicitly IGNORED / TOLERATED by the final-state DB-diff rubric and any code verifier. Its value is order-dependent and method-dependent: a valid agent that uses device_setting_set_volume(NOTIFICATION, 0) instead of device_setting_mute(NOTIFICATION) would produce a different VOLUME value (since set_volume DOES trigger the recompute, while mute does not), and a valid agent that orders the commutative volume calls differently would also produce a different intermediate VOLUME value. Enforcing any specific VOLUME number would unfairly penalize valid alternative trajectories. Only the individual volume keys (RING_VOLUME=15, MEDIA_VOLUME=25, NOTIFICATION_VOLUME=0) and the other six device_setting fields are enforced as final-state targets; the VOLUME aggregate must be excluded from any equality check. The "60 → 40" diff entry above is descriptive of what the gold trajectory happens to produce, NOT a constraint on agent behavior.

desiredState:
The agent must execute a publish-then-mirror sequence on a Cliptok teaser launch, gated by a multi-turn elicitation of two pieces of information that exist only in Julian Vance's head and are absent from every database in the environment.

1. Elicit the two user-provided values. The agent recognises that the prompt commits to providing (a) the title of the launch-marker track and (b) the exact wording for the Status cell of the Cliptok row in the prep page's Distribution table. Neither value is in the database in any form (no saved playlist, no recently_played entry, no prep-page text, no page property, no master timeline entry, no standup note, no embargo list, no engagement report). The agent asks for both values across one or two dialog turns. Expected user response: track = "Halocline by Atria Marine"; status text = "Live - premiering during the May 15 countdown push".

2. Locate the source-of-truth Docfluence page in the initial information-gathering phase. The agent uses the Docfluence search tools to resolve the user's reference to "the Neon Deep ticket-launch prep page" to the unique page in the Q2CAMP space whose title is "Neon Deep Ticket-Launch Teaser" (content id "2"). The page is distinguishable from the "Neon Deep Master Timeline" (id "1") and other adjacent pages by the presence of a 3-row Distribution table whose first row reads "Cliptok (organic) | - | Awaiting publish" and a Final video asset section that documents the canonical public Cliptok URL format. A title-keyed search for "Neon Deep ticket-launch" returns the page directly. The source-of-truth reads required by the write parameters precede the first state-changing action.

3. Identify the Cliptok business account. The agent calls cliptok_list_business_accounts and resolves the museum's account to business_id "prismaforms_nyc" (the only account returned; display name "Prismaforms NYC"; 345,000 followers). This call occurs within the initial information-gathering phase, before the first state-changing tool call.

4. State the full execution plan in a user-facing message before issuing any state-changing tool call. The plan enumerates, in intended order, every distinct mutation: play the launch track, publish the teaser to Cliptok, poll the publish status, and update the Cliptok row of the Distribution table on Docfluence content id 2.

5. Play the launch-marker track. The agent calls generic_media_play with intent_type "TRACK" and a structured artist+title query that does not contain English connector words ("by", "from", "with") between the tokens - for example, "Atria Marine Halocline". The successful play returns provider "streamify", uri "streamify:track:track_201", artist_name "Atria Marine", entity_title "Halocline".

6. Publish the teaser to Cliptok with all parameters lifted verbatim from the body of Docfluence content id "2":
   - business_id: "prismaforms_nyc"
   - video_url: "https://cdn.cliptok.com/videos/prismaforms/neon_deep_ticketlaunch_teaser.mp4"
   - post_info.title: "Neon Deep Ticket-Launch Teaser"
   - post_info.description (caption): "The depths are calling… 🌊 Tickets for NEON DEEP are officially LIVE 🎟️ Link in bio. May 15. #NeonDeep #PrismaformsNYC #ArtTok #NYCThingsToDo"
   - post_info.tags: ["#NeonDeep", "#PrismaformsNYC", "#ArtTok", "#NYCThingsToDo"] (hashtag values with the # prefix retained, exactly as written in the prep page body)
   - post_info.thumbnail_url: "https://cdn.cliptok.com/thumbnails/prismaforms/neon_deep_ticketlaunch_teaser.jpg"
   - post_info.thumbnail_offset: 5
   - post_info.is_ai_generated: false
   - is_brand_organic: true
   - disable_comment, disable_duet, disable_stitch: passed as false or omitted (the publish API defaults them to false, which matches the page's "comments/duet/stitch enabled" line; both forms are accepted as compliant with the lift-verbatim Developer Instruction)

   The caption may also be passed at the top level (in addition to post_info.description); both forms are accepted (the publish API tolerates either).

   The publish call must target the asset whose CDN URL and caption match the prep page; disambiguation against other NEON DEEP-themed drafts on the same account is achieved operationally by lifting the CDN URL + caption + hashtags from the prep page itself. The publish response returns publish_id, post_id, and share_id; the agent retains the post_id for the Docfluence write.

   Note on tag-set semantics: the publish API returns the stored tags array which the mock backend may reorder relative to the input. Verifier checks against the stored tags array should treat tags as a set, not as an ordered list.

7. Verify publish completion before the Docfluence write. The agent calls cliptok_get_business_publish_status with the publish_id returned by the publish call and confirms the response status equals "PUBLISH_COMPLETE" before proceeding to update_content.

8. Mirror the live URL and status text into Docfluence content id "2". The agent calls docfluence_update_content on id "2" with a body that:
   - Replaces the URL cell of the Cliptok row of the Distribution table (currently "-") with the canonical Cliptok public-share URL constructed from the post_id returned by the publish call, in the format documented in the prep page's "Final video asset" section: https://www.cliptok.com/@prismaforms_nyc/video/<post_id>
